examples.en: I worked all day, so my whole body aches.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날이면 할머니는 삭신 쑤신다고 하세요.
examples.en: On rainy days, Grandma says her whole body aches.

examples.ko: 이사를 마쳤더니 삭신에 힘이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: After finishing the move, my whole body has no strength left.
With this cold, even my whole body hurts.
My body is fine, but my mind is worn out.
I massaged my mother's aching body.

explain: 거의 '삭신이 쑤시다'처럼 몸이 아프고 결릴 때 써요. 어른들, 특히 나이 드신 분들이 많이 쓰는 정겨운 말이고, 젊은 사람은 '온몸이'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My whole body aches after sitting for so long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭신이 쑤시다'보다 더 일반적으로 아프다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general way to say the body aches than 삭신이 쑤시다.

phrases.en: The weather's bad, so my whole body aches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 여기저기가 욱신욱신 아프다는 느낌으로, 나이 드신 분들이 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys a throbbing ache all over the body, and older people often say it.

phrases.en: I caught a cold, so my whole body hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 사람들이 '삭신' 대신 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What younger people use more often instead of 삭신.

explain_en: It is used almost only in phrases like '삭신이 쑤시다' when your body aches. It is a familiar, warm word often used by older people, while younger people more often say '온몸이'.

t90.ax: I massaged my mother's aching body.

en: inside one's hand; within one's grasp

examples.en: The little bird fit snugly into my hand.

examples.ko: 요즘은 스마트폰 하나로 손안에서 은행 일을 다 봐요.
examples.en: These days, I handle all my banking in the palm of my hand with a single smartphone.
The sand in my hand slipped away.

examples.ko: 손안에 땀이 나서 펜이 자꾸 미끄러졌어요.
examples.en: My palm was sweaty, so the pen kept slipping.

examples.ko: 아이는 사탕을 손안에 꼭 쥐고 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was holding the candy tightly in their hand.

examples.ko: 동전을 손안에 감추고 마술을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: He hid a coin in his hand and showed me a magic trick.

explain: '손바닥'은 손의 평평한 면이고, '손안'은 손을 오므렸을 때 그 안쪽 공간에 가까워요. 보통 '손안에', '손안의'처럼 조사와 함께 쓰고 붙여 써요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 년 만에 시장을 손안에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: to take full control of something
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 쥐는 것이 아니라 어떤 힘이나 대상을 완전히 차지하고 마음대로 할 수 있게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean holding an object but gaining complete control over some power or target.
phrases.en_equiv: have something in the palm of one's hand

explain_en: '손바닥' is the flat surface of the hand, while '손안' is closer to the space inside the hand when you close it. It is usually written as one word and used with particles, as in '손안에' or '손안의'.

en: to shut one's teeth; to set one's teeth

examples.en: I clenched my teeth to bear the pain.
He clamped his mouth shut and held back his tears.
I gritted my teeth and ran to the end.

examples.ko: 악다문 입으로 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: With a tightly shut mouth, he said nothing.
He seemed angry and clenched his jaw.

examples.ko: 이를 악다물며 무거운 짐을 들어 올렸어요.
examples.en: I lifted the heavy load with gritted teeth.

explain: 입이나 이를 힘껏 꽉 다물 때 써요. 힘든 것을 참거나 굳게 각오할 때, 또는 화가 날 때 나오는 모습이에요. '다물다'가 ㄹ받침이라 '악다문'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요. 비슷한 '이를 악물다'도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I gritted my teeth to go all the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이를 악다물다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'ireul akdamulda' and used more often.

phrases.en: He clenched his mouth shut in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 대신 입이 목적어가 되어 입을 꽉 닫는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'mouth' as the object, it describes clamping the mouth shut.

phrases.en: I could feel firm resolve in his tightly shut mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악다물다'를 '악다문'으로 활용해서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form 'akdamun', used to describe a noun.

explain_en: Use it when you press your mouth or teeth tightly shut with force, such as enduring pain, resolving firmly, or being angry. 다물다 is an ㄹ-stem verb, so the ㄹ drops in forms like '악다문'. The similar '이를 악물다' is also common.

t90.ax: I clenched my teeth to bear the pain.

examples.ko: 아이가 잔병치레가 잦아서 병원에 자주 가요.
examples.en: My child gets sick often, so we go to the hospital a lot.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 어릴 때 잔병치레를 많이 했어요.
examples.en: My son was sick a lot when he was little.

examples.ko: 잔병치레 한 번 안 하고 겨울을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I got through the winter without being sick even once.
I suffer from one minor illness after another every change of season.

examples.ko: 잔병치레는 커 가면서 점점 줄어들 거예요.
examples.en: The frequent sickness will gradually decrease as they grow.
Since I started exercising, I no longer get sick often.

explain: '잔병'이 가벼운 병 자체라면, '잔병치레'는 그런 병을 자주 앓는 일을 가리켜요. 주로 아이나 몸이 약한 사람에게 쓰고 '잔병치레를 하다'가 기본 모양이에요.

phrases.en: My daughter hardly ever gets sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 아프지 않고 튼튼하다는 뜻이에요. 아이 건강을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one is sturdy and rarely falls ill; often used for children's health.

phrases.en: My younger sibling gets sick often every winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감기 같은 가벼운 병을 자주 앓는다는 뜻이에요. '잔병치레를 자주 하다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting minor illnesses like colds often; same meaning as '잔병치레를 자주 하다'.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 잔병치레하던 아이가 지금은 튼튼해졌어요.
phrases.en: The child who used to be sickly is now strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔병치레를 하다'를 한 동사처럼 줄인 말이에요. 어릴 때를 돌아볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened verb form of '잔병치레를 하다', often used when looking back on childhood.

explain_en: While '잔병' is the minor illness itself, '잔병치레' is the experience of getting such illnesses over and over. It is mostly used for children or people with a weak body, and the basic pattern is '잔병치레를 하다'.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 감기 특효약은 없다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said there is no miracle cure for colds.
There is still no wonder drug for this illness.
They say laughter is a miracle cure for stress.
Grandmother's love is the best remedy for me.

examples.ko: 광고에서 특효약처럼 말하는 제품은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful with products that are advertised like miracle cures.
That book felt like a cure for me.

explain: 약뿐 아니라 '웃음이 스트레스의 특효약이다'처럼 문제를 잘 풀어 주는 방법을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. '만병통치약'은 모든 병에 듣는 약이라는 더 큰 말이에요. 광고의 특효약 설명은 믿기 전에 확인해야 해요.

phrases.en: There is no cure-all in the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 병에 듣는다는 약을 말하고, '특효약'보다 범위가 훨씬 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medicine said to cure every illness; much broader in scope than 특효약.

phrases.en: People look for a miracle drug for losing weight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 쉽게 풀어 줄 방법을 찾을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when looking for an easy fix to a problem.

phrases.en: Exercise is a miracle cure for stress.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스트레스의 특효약'처럼 무엇을 잘 풀어 주는 방법을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively, as in 'a cure for stress', for something that solves a problem well.

explain_en: Besides real medicine, it is often used figuratively for something that solves a problem well, as in '웃음이 스트레스의 특효약이다'. '만병통치약' is a bigger word meaning a cure for every illness. You should check claims of a miracle cure in ads before believing them.

examples.ko: 밤에 아무도 없는데 누가 부르는 환청이 들렸어요.
examples.en: At night, with nobody there, I heard what sounded like someone calling me.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 환청까지 들리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm so tired that I feel like I'm even hearing things.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 진동 환청 때문에 자꾸 확인해요.
examples.en: I keep checking because I imagine my phone vibrating.

examples.ko: 그 소리는 환청이 아니라 진짜 옆집 소리였어요.
examples.en: That sound wasn't in my head; it was really the neighbor's noise.

examples.ko: 환청이 계속되면 병원에 가 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If you keep hearing things, it's good to see a doctor.

examples.ko: 환청 증상이 있는 사람은 전문가의 도움이 필요해요.
examples.en: People with symptoms of auditory hallucinations need professional help.

explain: 실제로 나지 않는 소리가 들리는 것을 말하고, 보통 '환청이 들리다'라고 써요. 일상에서는 피곤할 때 소리를 잘못 들은 느낌을 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요. 눈에 보이는 가짜 모습은 '환각'이나 '환영'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm so tired that I hear things that aren't there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 나지 않는 소리가 들린다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrasing for hearing sounds that aren't really there.
phrases.en_equiv: to hear things that aren't there

phrases.en: He said he hears voices that aren't there every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when the listener is the subject.

phrases.example: 약 때문에 환각이 나타날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Hallucinations can appear because of medication.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리뿐 아니라 눈에 보이는 가짜 모습까지 넓게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that covers false sights as well as sounds.

explain_en: It is the experience of hearing sounds that are not really there, usually said as '환청이 들리다'. In daily life people also use it lightly when they think they heard something because they are tired. Seeing things that aren't there is '환각' or '환영'.

examples.en: The old paper is curled up into a roll.
The marble rolled far away across the floor.

examples.ko: 얇은 김이 도르르 말려서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The thin seaweed sheet curls up, so it is hard to eat.

examples.ko: 아이가 이불을 도르르 말고 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The child is lying there rolled up in the blanket.
The toilet paper unrolled and piled up on the floor.

examples.ko: 동전이 책상 아래로 도르르 굴러 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The coin rolled off and fell under the desk.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 굴러가거나 종이처럼 얇은 것이 말리는 모양에 써요. '데굴데굴'은 좀 더 크게 구르는 느낌이라 도르르와 느낌이 달라요. 주로 '도르르 말리다', '도르르 구르다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The wet paper curled up into a roll as it dried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 천처럼 얇은 것이 스스로 말릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for thin things like paper curling on their own.

phrases.example: 작은 구슬이 도르르 굴러서 책상 밑으로 갔어요.
phrases.en: The little marble rolled away under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 가벼운 것이 가볍게 구르는 소리와 모양을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the light sound and look of a small thing rolling.

phrases.en: I rolled up the poster and put it in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일부러 종이를 말 때에도 써서 말리는 모양을 생생하게 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also works when a person rolls paper on purpose, making the motion vivid.

explain_en: It describes small, light things rolling along or thin things like paper curling up. '데굴데굴' feels bigger and heavier, so the feeling is different. It is mostly used as '도르르 말리다' or '도르르 구르다'.

examples.ko: 불이 나가서 방이 완전히 암흑이 됐어요.
examples.en: The power went out and the room became pitch dark.
It's pitch dark inside the cave, so you need a flashlight.

examples.ko: 전쟁 때는 암흑 같은 시간을 보냈다고 해요.
examples.en: They say people lived through dark times during the war.
That movie begins in darkness.
Everything went pitch black before my eyes.
The whole city was plunged into darkness by the blackout.

explain: 암흑은 빛이 전혀 없는 어둠이에요. '어둠'보다 더 짙고, '암흑기'처럼 힘든 시대를 말할 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '깜깜하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 긴 암흑기를 지나 다시 일어났어요.
phrases.en: That country rose again after a long dark age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들고 희망이 없던 시기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a long period of hardship without hope.

explain_en: 암흑 is darkness with no light at all, deeper than 어둠. It also describes hard times, as in 암흑기 (dark age). In daily talk people say 깜깜하다 more often.

en: to look threatening; to look tough

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼굴이 우락부락해서 처음엔 무서웠어요.
examples.en: His face looked so tough that I was scared at first.

examples.ko: 우락부락한 팔뚝의 아저씨가 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: A man with thick, rough-looking arms carried my bags.
He looks tough, but he likes puppies.
My older brother worked out and his body became beefy.
The tough-looking guard greeted me first.
His voice is rough too, so the children are afraid of him.

explain: 생김새나 체격이 거칠고 억세 보일 때 써요. 외모를 평가하는 말이라 앞에서 직접 말하면 실례일 수 있어요. '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'처럼 겉모습과 다르다고 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: He has a tough face, but a warm heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴 생김새를 말할 때 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form for describing a face.

phrases.en: That security guard looks tough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전체적인 생김새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone's overall appearance.

phrases.en: Since I grew a beard, my face looks rugged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that something looks that way on the outside.

explain_en: It describes a face or build that looks rough and tough. Since it comments on appearance, saying it to someone's face can be rude. It is often used to contrast looks with personality, as in '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'.

examples.en: My grandfather has dignity even without speaking.
The king entered with a majestic stride.

examples.ko: 사자는 위엄 있는 모습으로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The lion stands with a majestic look.

examples.ko: 새 교장 선생님은 위엄을 지키려고 노력해요.
examples.en: The new principal tries to keep an air of authority.
You can feel a sense of grandeur from that old building.
I practiced speaking with authority.

explain: '위엄'은 사람이나 대상에서 느껴지는, 함부로 대하기 어려운 무게감이에요. '위엄 있다', '위엄을 지키다'처럼 써요. '권위'와 비슷하지만 '위엄'은 겉모습이나 태도에서 느껴지는 힘에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: I can feel dignity in that person's voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말투에서 무게감이 전해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sense of weight comes through someone's manner or voice.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a sense of dignity

phrases.en: Even when I was angry, I tried to keep my dignity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체면과 무게를 잃지 않으려 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when trying not to lose one's composure or stature.

phrases.en: If you only laugh, you seem to lack authority.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위엄 있다'의 반대로, 무게감이 느껴지지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '위엄 있다', used when no sense of authority comes across.

explain_en: '위엄' is the weight a person or thing carries that makes it hard to treat lightly. Use it as '위엄 있다' or '위엄을 지키다'. Close to '권위', but '위엄' leans toward the power felt in appearance and manner.

examples.en: It was such a tempting offer that I thought about it for a moment.

examples.ko: 빵집에서 나는 유혹적인 냄새를 그냥 지나칠 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't just walk past the tempting smell coming from the bakery.

examples.ko: 광고 속 모델의 표정이 너무 유혹적이에요.
examples.en: The model's expression in the ad is so enticing.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 먹는 라면은 유혹적인 음식이지만 건강에는 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Ramen late at night is a tempting food, but it's bad for your health.
Be careful not to fall for that enticing way of talking.

examples.ko: 친구가 보낸 유혹적인 여행 계획에 마음이 흔들려요.
examples.en: My friend's tempting travel plan is making me waver.

explain: '매력적'은 그냥 마음이 끌린다는 좋은 느낌이고, '유혹적'은 넘어갈 것 같아서 조금 조심해야 하는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '유혹적인 제안', '유혹적인 냄새'처럼 명사 앞에서 '-인'을 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: That offer is really tempting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 서술어로 쓸 때는 '-이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: At the end of a sentence it takes '-이다' as a predicate.

phrases.en: Those words sounded very tempting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 말이 마음을 끌 때 '-으로 들리다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-으로 들리다' when what you hear pulls at you.

phrases.en: A seductive voice came from the radio.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 끌어당기는 느낌의 목소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a voice that has a pulling, alluring quality.

explain_en: '매력적' just means attractive in a good way, while '유혹적' carries a feeling that you might give in, so you should be a little careful. It is usually used before a noun with '-인', as in '유혹적인 제안' or '유혹적인 냄새'.

en: to be desolate and silent; to be lonely and still

examples.en: The dawn street was so quiet it felt desolate.

examples.ko: 이사 가고 나니 집이 적막해서 허전해요.
examples.en: After moving, the house is so silent that it feels empty.

examples.ko: 겨울 바다는 사람이 없어 적막한 느낌이에요.
examples.en: The winter sea has no people, so it feels desolate and still.
On nights that feel too silent, I play music.
After the children left, the school became desolately quiet.
I heard the temple in the mountains is hushed even in the daytime.

explain: '조용하다'가 소리가 적다는 뜻이라면, '적막하다'는 거기에 쓸쓸하고 외로운 느낌이 더해져요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: In the silent night, I could only hear the clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used before a noun.

phrases.en: The store with its lights off looks desolate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 느껴지는 쓸쓸함을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the lonely feeling that comes from appearance.

phrases.en: With the kids around, the house isn't lonely and still.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸쓸하지 않고 활기가 있다는 뜻을 부정으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it's lively rather than lonely.

explain_en: While '조용하다' simply means there is little noise, '적막하다' adds a lonely, desolate feeling. It sounds more natural in writing or storytelling than in everyday conversation.

en: to be slow; to be sluggish

examples.en: The negotiations have been dragging on for months.
The construction is so slow that the residents are angry.
Everyone is worn out because of the sluggish meeting.
I don't know why the project is so sluggish.

examples.ko: 일이 지지부진하게 진행되면 팀 분위기도 나빠져요.
examples.en: When work proceeds sluggishly, the team's mood gets worse too.
The matter that had been dragging on was finally resolved.

explain: 그냥 '느리다'가 아니라 일이 잘 나아가지 않고 답답하게 늘어진다는 느낌이에요. 주로 협상, 공사, 논의, 수사처럼 일의 진행에 쓰고 '지지부진한 ~'의 형태로 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: I'm worried because of the sluggish negotiations.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요. 협상, 공사, 논의 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies a noun, and it fits words like negotiation, construction and discussion.

phrases.example: 올해는 작년과 달리 일이 지지부진하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Unlike last year, work isn't dragging this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 일이 잘 나아가고 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the work is moving along well.

phrases.en: The project is dragging on slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 답답하게 늘어지며 계속되는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe something that keeps going in a frustratingly slow way.

explain_en: It is not just 'slow' but carries the frustrating feeling that something is not moving forward and keeps dragging. It is mostly used for how a matter progresses, such as negotiations, construction, discussions and investigations, and you often hear it as '지지부진한 ~' in the news.

t90.ax: I don't know why the project is so sluggish.

en: to be clear; to be pure

examples.ko: 그 가수는 청아한 목소리로 노래를 불러요.
examples.en: That singer sings in a clear, pure voice.
The bell of the mountain temple rang out clear and pure.

examples.ko: 목소리가 청아해서 아나운서 같다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I was told I sound like an announcer because my voice is clear and pure.

examples.ko: 청아하고 맑은 피리 소리에 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: The clear, pure sound of the flute put my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 그 아이의 웃음소리는 청아하다고 할 만해요.
examples.en: That child's laughter can be called clear and pure.

examples.ko: 청아하지만 힘 있는 목소리가 극장에 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A voice that was clear yet strong spread through the theater.

explain: 소리, 특히 목소리·새소리·종소리가 맑고 깨끗할 때 써요. '맑다'는 물·하늘·소리에 다 쓰지만, 청아하다는 귀로 듣는 소리에 주로 써요. 글에서 칭찬하는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '목소리가 맑아요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: That singer is famous for a clear, pure voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로 목소리를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used to praise a voice.

phrases.en: The bell rang out clearly and purely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 퍼지는 모습을 글처럼 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a literary way for how a sound spreads.

phrases.en: That child's voice is clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청아하다보다 쉽고 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 청아하다 and more natural in conversation.

explain_en: It describes sound, especially voices, birdsong and bells, that is clear and clean. '맑다' is used for water, sky and sound, but '청아하다' is mostly for sounds the ear hears. It is a complimentary word used in writing, while in daily talk people say '목소리가 맑아요'.

t90.ax: That singer sings in a clear, pure voice.

en: to be calm; to be cool; to be self-possessed

examples.en: Even after seeing his exam results, he stayed calm.
How can you say that so casually?
I was shocked that he lied with such a straight face.
I tried to stay composed even in a crisis.
How can you be so unruffled?

examples.ko: 발표 전에는 태연해 보여도 속으로 많이 떨려요.
examples.en: Before a presentation I may look calm, but inside I'm very nervous.

explain: '침착하다'는 당황하지 않고 차분하게 행동하는 좋은 느낌이 있고, '태연하다'는 놀라거나 미안해할 만한 일에도 아무렇지 않은 듯한 모습을 말해요. 그래서 때로는 '뻔뻔하다'는 비판이 섞이기도 해요. '태연하게', '태연히'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I was scared, but I acted unfazed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속마음과 달리 아무렇지 않은 모습을 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing a calm face that doesn't match one's real feelings.

phrases.en: I look fine outside, but inside I am not calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 마음이 편하지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means one does not feel at ease.

phrases.en: He sat down calmly as if nothing was wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 동작을 꾸며요. '태연하게'보다 조금 글 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form modifies an action; it is slightly more literary than 태연하게.

explain_en: '침착하다' has a positive feel of staying composed and acting calmly, while '태연하다' describes looking unbothered even about something that should surprise or embarrass you. So it can carry a hint of criticism, like being shameless. It is often used as '태연하게' or '태연히'.

t90.ax: How can you be so unruffled?
